summary: Fast, widely used gradient boosting library for tabular data that runs on one machine or scales across Spark, Dask and Kubernetes.

heroCommands.command: See the XGBoost documentation at xgboost.readthedocs.io

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) is an optimized, distributed gradient boosting library. It implements parallel tree boosting (also known as GBDT or GBM) to solve many data science problems quickly and accurately, and the same code runs on distributed environments such as Kubernetes, Hadoop, SGE, Dask, Spark and PySpark.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many prediction problems on tables of data (churn, fraud, pricing, ranking) are best solved with boosted trees. XGBoost gives a fast, proven implementation that scales to billions of examples.
whoFor: Data scientists working with tabular data
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for speed, accuracy on structured data and the ability to scale the same code from a laptop to a cluster.
requirements: See the official installation guide for your language and platform

overview: The README itself doesn't list install commands; it points to the official documentation at xgboost.readthedocs.io, which covers installation, tutorials and the API.
XGBoost focuses on efficiency, flexibility and portability. It originates from a research project at the University of Washington (Chen and Guestrin, KDD 2016).
Demos and resources are in the repo's demo folder. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Not for images or text out of the box
